quizzes.title: Polygamy rates and types
quizzes.passage: Polygamy is the subject of a new law in Assam, where the state assembly has passed the Prohibition of Polygamy Bill 2025 to introduce strict penalties against such practices. The topic sits within the wider field of marriage and family law in India, where personal laws for different communities treat marriage in different ways. The prevalence of polygamy is measured through a national health survey, which reports figures for the country as a whole, for individual states and for religious communities. Assam's figure is set against the national average, and the state's religious communities are reported separately. The survey covers currently married women in a particular age band and records whether their husband has other wives besides themselves. Such figures allow comparison between states and between religious groups across the country. The Bill is framed as an effort to eliminate polygamous practices, and its provisions extend to residents of Assam as well as to certain people who engage in polygamous marriages outside the state. Its scope therefore reaches beyond marriages performed inside the state. The statistics form the background to the legislative debate in the state, and they are cited alongside the provisions of the Bill. Readers who follow the topic will also see how the law interacts with the marriage statutes that operate across the country.

questions.q: What is the NFHS-5 (2019-21) polygamy rate reported for Assam?
questions.explanation: Assam's rate is 2.4 per cent, compared with the national figure of 1.4 per cent.

questions.q: According to the same survey, which religious group in Assam records the higher rate?
questions.explanation: Muslims in Assam record 3.6 per cent against 1.8 per cent for Hindus.

questions.q: Which term describes a system in which one woman has several husbands?
questions.explanation: Polyandry is the arrangement in which one woman has several husbands.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Assam's polygamy rate is above the national average.
Reason (R): The national rate for Christians is above that for Muslims.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, but the Christian-Muslim comparison does not explain Assam's rate.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
List I: I. Hindus   II. Muslims   III. Christians   IV. Sikhs
List II: A. 2.1 per cent   B. 0.5 per cent   C. 1.3 per cent   D. 1.9 per cent
questions.explanation: Nationally, Hindus are 1.3, Muslims 1.9, Christians 2.1 and Sikhs 0.5 per cent.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The national rate for Others is higher than the national rate for Muslims.
II. Sikhs record a higher national rate than Hindus.
III. Assam's rate is higher than Meghalaya's.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Only statement I is correct, since Others record 2.5 per cent against 1.9 per cent for Muslims.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. Polyandry means one man has several wives.
II. Hindus have a national polygamy rate of 1.3 per cent.
III. The national rate for Christians is 1.3 per cent.
questions.explanation: Only statement II is correct, since the national rate for Hindus is 1.3 per cent.

questions.q: What is the NFHS-5 (2019-21) polygamy rate for India as a whole, in per cent? (number only)
questions.explanation: The national polygamy rate in NFHS-5 is 1.4 per cent.

questions.q: What is the NFHS-5 polygamy rate for Assam, in per cent? (number only)
questions.explanation: Assam's NFHS-5 rate is 2.4 per cent.

questions.q: What is the NFHS-5 polygamy rate for Muslims in Assam, in per cent? (number only)
questions.explanation: Muslims in Assam record 3.6 per cent in NFHS-5.

questions.q: What term describes a marital system in which one man has several wives? (one word)
questions.explanation: Polygyny is the arrangement in which one man has multiple wives.

questions.q: What is the NFHS-5 national polygamy rate for Sikhs, in per cent? (number only)
questions.explanation: The national rate for Sikhs in NFHS-5 is 0.5 per cent.

questions.q: What is the NFHS-5 national polygamy rate for Christians, in per cent? (number only)
questions.explanation: The national rate for Christians in NFHS-5 is 2.1 per cent.

questions.q: Which national survey, covering 2019-21, reports these polygamy rates? (abbreviation)
questions.explanation: The rates come from the fifth National Family Health Survey, abbreviated NFHS-5.

quizzes.title: Personal laws and marriage
quizzes.passage: Marriage in India is governed by personal laws that differ according to religion, so the legal position on a second marriage is not the same for every community. Statutes differ on whether a second marriage during the subsistence of the first is treated as wrongful, while other personal laws leave room for more than one spouse. The legal framework is part of the background to the Assam Prohibition of Polygamy Bill 2025, which the state assembly has passed. Criminal law also addresses marrying again during the lifetime of a spouse, under a code enacted in 2023. The Bill applies to residents of Assam and also covers individuals engaged in polygamous marriages outside the state, which gives it a reach beyond the state's own population. The Uniform Civil Code is the idea of a common set of personal laws that would apply to all citizens irrespective of religious affiliations. Several judgments of the Supreme Court have discussed the need for reform of personal laws over the decades. The Law Commission has also examined the subject in its consultation report. The Bill's objective is to eliminate polygamous practices across India, not only in Assam. The debate on uniformity has continued for many decades. Each of these points forms part of the wider context in which the state's Bill is discussed.

questions.q: Which Act permits polygamy among Muslims in India?
questions.explanation: The Shariat Application Act of 1937 is the Act under which polygamy is permitted for Muslims.

questions.q: Under the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, what is a second marriage contracted while the first subsists?
questions.explanation: Contracting a second marriage while the first subsists is a punishable offence under the Hindu Marriage Act.

questions.q: What can be done with Shariat marriages that violate Fundamental Rights?
questions.explanation: Marriages under the Shariat Act that violate Fundamental Rights can be legally challenged.

questions.q: In which year was the Muslim Personal Law (Shariat) Application Act enacted?
questions.explanation: The Shariat Application Act was enacted in 1937.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The Muslim Personal Law (Shariat) Application Act, 1937 prohibits polygamy.
Reason (R): Polygamy is permitted under the Muslim Personal Law (Shariat) Application Act, 1937.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The Shariat Act permits polygamy, so A is false while R is true.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. Bigamy is prohibited for Hindus under the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.
II. The Shariat Act, 1937 prohibits polygamy among Muslims.
III. Marriages under the Shariat Act that violate Fundamental Rights can be legally challenged.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are correct, while II is wrong because the Shariat Act permits polygamy.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. The Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 prohibits bigamy for Hindus.
II. The Special Marriage Act, 1954 permits polygamy.
III. A second marriage during the subsistence of the first is a punishable offence under the Hindu Marriage Act.
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are correct, while II is wrong because the Special Marriage Act does not permit polygamy.

questions.q: In which year was the Hindu Marriage Act enacted? (year)
questions.explanation: The Hindu Marriage Act was enacted in 1955.

questions.q: In which year was the Muslim Personal Law (Shariat) Application Act enacted? (year)
questions.explanation: The Shariat Application Act was enacted in 1937.

questions.q: What term describes marrying again while a first marriage subsists, which the Hindu Marriage Act prohibits for Hindus? (one word)
questions.explanation: Bigamy is the term for marrying again while a first marriage subsists.

questions.q: Under the 1937 Act, polygamy is permitted for which community's personal law? (one word)
questions.explanation: The Shariat Application Act of 1937 permits polygamy under Muslim personal law.

questions.q: What is the abbreviation of the 2023 criminal code under which marrying again during a spouse's lifetime is an offence? (abbreviation)
questions.explanation: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 is abbreviated BNS and makes marrying again during a spouse's lifetime an offence.

questions.q: What term describes the constitutional rights against which Shariat marriages can be tested? (two words)
questions.explanation: Shariat marriages that violate Fundamental Rights can be legally challenged.

questions.q: How many years separate the enactment of the Muslim Personal Law (Shariat) Application Act (1937) and the Hindu Marriage Act (1955)? (number of years)
questions.explanation: The gap is 1955 minus 1937, which is 18 years.
